subject.title: Output sanitizer: improve duplicate detection for same-line and partial duplicates

question: How broad should OpenClaw's user-facing output sanitizer be allowed to get when removing partial or near-duplicate assistant text?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but partial or near-duplicate removal can delete intentional repetition; maintainer intent is needed to choose the heuristic boundary before implementation.

options.title: Conservative adjacent-only repair
options.body: Handle the glued final-tag repeat and explicitly supported adjacent same-line or single-newline exact duplicates with regression tests that preserve normal repetition.

options.title: Broader partial-duplicate sanitizer
options.body: Allow substring or near-duplicate removal, accepting higher false-positive risk and requiring stronger tests for quoted and user-requested repeated text.

options.title: Wait for broad normalizer PR
options.body: Defer this issue until the larger visible-output normalizer work has a settled shape and merge path.

recommendation.title: Conservative adjacent-only repair
recommendation.body: Handle the glued final-tag repeat and explicitly supported adjacent same-line or single-newline exact duplicates with regression tests that preserve normal repetition.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest routing candidate from sanitizer introduction history and prior issue review context.
